title: esp: add decryption support for ChaCha20-Poly1305-IIV and AES-GCM-IIV ciphers
description: This patch adds ESP decryption support for ChaCha20-Poly1305 (with and without Implicit Initialization Vector) and AES-GCM (with Implicit Initialization Vector) as per RFC 8750. Ciphers with IIV also use a 4 byte salt to form the nonce which is appended to the key (see section 2 of RFC 7634). ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption is commonly used in the communication between iPhone and Apple Watch. This also adds a protocol type "Any" to the ESP SAs to allow decryption of ESP payloads without an IP header.

Hi Alexis, for ChaCha20-Poly1305 (without IIV) I verified against the example capture in RFC 7634 (see attachment). You can use the following parameters in the ESP preferences to reproduce:

- SPI: 0x01020304
- Encryption: ChaCha20 with Poly1305 [RFC 7634]
- Encryption Key: 0x808182838485868788898a8b8c8d8e8f909192939495969798999a9b9c9d9e9fa0a1a2a3

For the IIV mode (AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305) I only have captures which contain sensitive data and I'm not aware of any open implementations which I could use to create an example capture.

[rfc7634-example.snoop](/uploads/87137503e062660a88d9a86468672bad/rfc7634-example.snoop)

LGTM

@johnthacker, it is good for use of memcpy/memset ? (or need to use tvb_...)
It's good, because it's coming from the UAT (and there are checks to make sure it's the proper length.)
